display.purpose: The hero line only, in display capitals.

headline.purpose: Each section head, in display capitals, two or three lines.

claim.purpose: A capability's name, in display capitals, between the section head and the prose.

wordmark.purpose: The brand name beside the mark.

title.purpose: A step head in the quick start, in Onest.

lead.purpose: The line under a head that says what the region does.

caption.purpose: The note under a demonstration, in muted ink.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: A control's face and a selected tab.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: A step card, an open FAQ item.

shadows.name: table
shadows.purpose: The plane every demonstration lies on.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: A recessed trough for tabs, rails and tables, and a pressed quiet button.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: The edge of every plane, in place of a border.

shadows.name: gold-button-hover
shadows.purpose: The primary button lifted 1px on hover.

shadows.name: gold-button-active
shadows.purpose: The primary button sunk 1px on press.

shadows.name: mock-window
shadows.purpose: The hero window, which stands higher than any table.

shadows.name: nav-stuck
shadows.purpose: The nav bar after the page scrolls 8px.

shadows.name: marker-glow
shadows.purpose: A small gold square or dot that glows.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default curve for state changes, lands and reveals.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Curve for sweeps, clip reveals and pulses that go both ways.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Buttons, tabs and links change state in 160ms.

motion.name: surface
motion.purpose: FAQ items, the stuck nav and tab fills settle in this time.

motion.name: scene
motion.purpose: A panel arrives, a view switches or a card lands.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: A block settles from 60% opacity and 8px low, once.

motion.name: sweep
motion.purpose: The proposal switch's light beam and clip reveal.

motion.name: canvas-fade
motion.purpose: A shader canvas fades in after its first frame.

motion.name: type-step
motion.purpose: The hero agent line types out.

motion.name: spark
motion.purpose: A spark draws each line of the hero drawing.

motion.name: autoplay
motion.purpose: The proposal switch alternates while it is on screen and untouched.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every CSS animation and transition collapses to this.

components.name: Gold Button

components.css: .ds-btn-gold { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius-control); font: 600 0.9375rem/1 var(--font-body); letter-spacing: -0.005em; color: var(--gold-ink); background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--gold-top), var(--gold-bottom)); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 oklch(1 0.02 90 / 0.55), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--gold-edge), 0 1px 0 oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.8), 0 6px 16px -6px oklch(0.55 0.12 75 / 0.55); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 160ms var(--ease-out), box-shadow 160ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-btn-gold:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 oklch(1 0.02 90 / 0.6), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--gold-edge), 0 2px 0 oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.8), 0 12px 28px -8px oklch(0.6 0.13 78 / 0.6); } .ds-btn-gold:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 3px oklch(0.45 0.1 70 / 0.6), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--gold-edge); } .ds-btn-gold:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold-mark); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Quiet Button

components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius-control); font: 600 0.9375rem/1 var(--font-body); letter-spacing: -0.005em; color: var(--ink); background: var(--raised); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--highlight), 0 1px 0 oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.7), 0 2px 6px -1px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.5), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 160ms var(--ease-out), background-color 160ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { background: var(--slab); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-quiet:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px oklch(0.04 0.004 75 / 0.6), inset 0 -1px 0 var(--highlight); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold-mark); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Segmented Tabs

components.css: .ds-tabs { display: inline-flex; gap: 2px; padding: 3px; border-radius: var(--radius-panel); background: var(--well); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px oklch(0.04 0.004 75 / 0.6), inset 0 -1px 0 var(--highlight); } .ds-tab { height: 32px; padding: 0 14px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius-control); background: transparent; font: 600 0.875rem/1 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink-muted); cursor: pointer; transition: color 160ms var(--ease-out), background-color 160ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } .ds-tab[aria-pressed='true'] { background: var(--raised); color: var(--ink); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--highlight), 0 1px 0 oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.7), 0 2px 6px -1px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.5), inset 0 -2px 0 var(--gold-mark); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold-mark); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Lit Table
components.description: The plane a demonstration lies on, in a chrome tray with a plane stage inside.
components.html: A real renderer drawing lies here.
components.css: .ds-table { padding: 6px; border-radius: var(--radius-table); background: var(--chrome); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--highlight), 0 2px 0 oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.6), 0 24px 48px -16px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.75), 0 64px 120px -48px oklch(0.04 0.006 75 / 0.9), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); } .ds-stage { display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 160px; border-radius: var(--radius-panel); background: var(--plane); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); } .ds-stage-note { margin: 0; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink-muted); }

components.name: Stage Card

Your agent states it

No x, no y, no width. Git reviews it like code.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; padding: 20px; border-radius: var(--radius-table); background: var(--plane); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--highlight), 0 1px 1px oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.6), 0 12px 24px -8px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.6), 0 32px 64px -24px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.7), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font: 600 1rem/1.4 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink); } .ds-card-code { margin: 0; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: var(--radius-panel); background: oklch(0.155 0.005 75); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); font: 400 0.78rem/1.7 var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink); overflow-x: auto; } .ds-ps { color: var(--gold-mark); } .ds-card-note { margin: 0; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink-muted); }

components.name: Status Chips

components.name: FAQ Item
components.description: A closed plane with a gold plus. Open, it rises to the card tone and the plus turns into a minus.
components.html:
Can I move a box?

No, and that is the point. Fix the meaning and the renderer redraws it.
components.css: .ds-faq { border-radius: var(--radius-panel); background: var(--plane); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); transition: background-color 200ms var(--ease-out), box-shadow 200ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-faq[open] { background: var(--card); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--highlight), 0 1px 1px oklch(0.06 0.004 75 / 0.6), 0 12px 24px -8px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.6), 0 32px 64px -24px oklch(0.06 0.006 75 / 0.7), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule); } .ds-faq summary { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 18px 20px; font: 600 1.0625rem/1.4 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink); cursor: pointer; list-style: none; } .ds-faq summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } .ds-faq summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold-mark); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-sign { position: relative; flex: none; width: 14px; height: 14px; } .ds-sign::before, .ds-sign::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 6px; width: 14px; height: 2px; border-radius: 1px; background: var(--gold-mark); transition: rotate 220ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-sign::after { rotate: 90deg; } .ds-faq[open] .ds-sign::after { rotate: 0deg; } .ds-faq p { margin: 0; padding: 0 20px 20px; max-width: 40em; font: 400 1.0625rem/1.6 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink-body); }

Read a system you did not write.

Archboard joins the model to the code and to its Git history. See where the design costs the most before anyone changes it.
components.css: .ds-head { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 7fr) minmax(0, 5fr); align-items: end; gap: 24px 64px; } .ds-h2 { margin: 0; max-width: 14ch; font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 780; font-size: clamp(2.6rem, 6.4vw, 4.75rem); line-height: 0.92; letter-spacing: 0.012em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink); text-wrap: balance; } .ds-lead { margin: 0; font: 400 clamp(1.0625rem, 1.4vw, 1.1875rem)/1.6 var(--font-body); color: var(--ink-body); text-wrap: pretty; }

narrative.northStar: The Lit Drafting Table at Night
narrative.overview:
The site is one long page in a dark room. Warm graphite planes stack under a light from above. Each plane has a lit top edge, a thin contact line and a soft warm shadow beneath it. Real drawings from the Archboard renderer lie on these planes and bring every colour the page has. The page claims that nobody places a box, so the renderer's drawings carry the proof and the chrome stays quiet.

One gold does the choosing. It marks the brand, the one action of a region, and what is selected. The type is tall condensed capitals for what a region is about, plain sans for every other word, and mono for commands, paths and counts. The values come from the renderer's dark theme in `packages/renderer/assets/theme.css`, and the type scale belongs to the site. The product's shell is a different surface with a light theme and keeps its own record at the repository root.

The build carries out the direction contract as written. The hero is left-aligned over a WebGL lamp and grid. A mock Archboard window in perspective holds the real example-shop drawing and builds itself line by line while real CLI commands type out. Each later section uses a different demonstration form: a sortable table, tabs, a switch, two panes, a timeline, a player, a zoom, a claim. The owner rejects three things. The first is the category default: a centered hero over a flat screenshot, then a grid of same-size icon cards. The others are a light theme and any label above a heading.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only. `color-scheme: dark` is set in the stylesheet and in a meta tag.
Planes, not lines. Depth comes from stacked tones, a lit top edge and a shadow, and edges are inset rings, not borders.
One gold in a few finishes. Every other colour in the page is state, kind or the renderer's own.
Display capitals for section heads and feature claims. Sans for prose. Mono for data.
Left-aligned composition. Only the closing call is centered.
Light moves along lines: a lamp pool, traffic on the grid, and sparks that draw lines. Nothing moves for decoration alone.
Every drawing is real renderer output.

rules.name: The One Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold marks the brand, the one primary action of a region, and what is chosen. No second accent hue exists. Do not use gold for decoration beyond the small square markers, prompts and glows that the build already uses.

rules.name: The Brights Mean Something Rule
rules.body: Green, orange, red and lime appear only where they mean added, changed, removed and live. The ten kind brights appear on kind chips, inside drawings and in the three small data marks above. The comparison table marks Archboard with a gold tint, never with green.

rules.name: The Quiet Ink Rule
rules.body: Faint ink is below the Lc 60 floor for secondary text. Use it for decoration, wait states, line numbers and rings. Never set a sentence or an answer in it.

rules.name: The Dark Only Rule
rules.body: The site has one theme. Do not add a light scheme or a theme switch. The browser chrome colour in the head (`#090806`) is a hand-set hex a little under the floor.

rules.name: The Tall Capitals Rule
rules.body: Display capitals name what a region is about: the hero line, section heads (h2) and feature claims (h3). Three narrow exceptions exist. The wordmark is display capitals. The language belt sets the languages the code check reads as display words. A module's name inside a demonstration of the product keeps the product's display title (the mock inspector and the interface comparison). Everything else is Onest: buttons, tabs, labels, table heads, captions.

rules.name: The Head Leads Rule
rules.body: A heading starts its region. No label, kicker, eyebrow or tag sits above a heading. The owner bans them. A line of words beside a belt, such as "The code check reads", labels the belt and sits level with it, not over a heading.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Mono sets commands, paths, counts and code. It never sets a heading or a label for a control.

rules.name: The Lit Table Rule
rules.body: Every plane carries all three of a lit top edge, a contact line and a soft shadow, or it carries none. A flat plane gets its edge from the hairline ring alone. The only zero-blur offset shadows are the 1px to 2px contact lines under a plane. Do not add a larger hard offset shadow.

rules.name: The Tray And Trough Rule
rules.body: A demonstration sits in a tray with a recessed trough or a plane inside. Selection raises a piece out of a trough and marks it with a 2px gold underline set inside its face.

rules.name: The Untouched Picture Rule
rules.body: The renderer draws a picture, and the page lays no gold, shadow or filter over it. The page can dim or light parts through the renderer's own classes, move whole parts, and ring the one card that invites a click.

rules.name: The Real Output Rule
rules.body: Every diagram is real renderer output, drawn in the dark theme from the example shop or from Archboard's own model. Never draw, trace, edit or imitate one by hand. Never use a screenshot of a mock or a generated image. A drawing that looks wrong is a renderer bug. Fix the renderer and draw it again.

rules.name: The Spark Order Rule
rules.body: A picture builds in one order: the cards land, a spark draws each line, then the traffic runs. Lines never appear all at once. This repeats the product's own Spark Rule. With reduced motion, everything is there at once.

rules.name: The Pause Rule
rules.body: Motion carries meaning, and it stops once nobody can see it. Every loop runs only while its element is on screen and the tab is visible. The fields, the orb, the narration and the proposal switch's autoplay do this through one helper, `whileVisible`. A CSS loop sits inside an element marked `data-loop`, and `pauseLoopsOffscreen` pauses its animations while that element is off screen. Moving content offers a way to stop it: the language belt has a Show all control that stops it and wraps every language, and with reduced motion it shows the wrapped list from the start. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, a shader draws one still frame. Scroll-driven tilt and parallax turn off. Autoplay and narration do not start. A global rule cuts every CSS animation and transition to 0.01ms and one iteration. A new loop follows both.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: Content is visible without script. With script, a revealed block starts at 60% opacity and 8px low, settles over 700ms with the ease-out curve, and does so once. A reader who scrolls fast never meets an empty band.

dos: Do keep the page dark only. Set every new plane from the Night Floor to Slab ladder.
Do spend gold on the brand, the one primary action of a region, and what is chosen.
Do set section heads and feature claims in the display face in capitals, and every other word in Onest.
Do open every region with its heading. Put the lead beside or under it.
Do set commands, paths and counts in Maple Mono.
Do build each plane with a lit top edge, a contact line and a soft warm shadow, and edge it with an inset hairline ring.
Do show every diagram as renderer output, and name what it shows in the alt text.
Do keep green, orange and red for added, changed, removed and live.
Do run every new loop only while visible, and give it a still state for reduced motion.
Do give each demonstration its own form, and keep the composition left-aligned.
Do label mock interface data as an example.
donts: Do not add a light theme, a theme switch or a second accent hue.
Do not put a label, kicker, eyebrow or tag above a heading.
Do not set body text, buttons, tabs, table heads or captions in display capitals.
Do not draw, trace or imitate a diagram by hand, and do not use a screenshot or a generated image in place of renderer output.
Do not use hard offset shadows larger than a 2px contact line, side stripes on cards, panels or list items, emoji or glyph icons.
Do not set a sentence or an answer in Faint Ink.
Do not use state colours or kind brights as decoration.
Do not lay gold, shadow or blur over a renderer drawing.
Do not build a grid of same-size icon cards, or a centered hero over a flat screenshot.
Do not edit or reuse the product's root `DESIGN.md`. It records the light application shell, which is a different surface.
